import pytest


class TestSuite(unittest.TestCase):
    # test_pos has a run of six: assert, self.assertEqual, self.assertTrue, a
    # with pytest.raises, self.assertIn and a pytest.raises call.
    def test_pos(self):
        got = compute()
        assert got == 1
        self.assertEqual(got, 1)
        self.assertTrue(got)
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            compute()
        self.assertIn(1, got)
        pytest.raises(E, compute)
        print("not an assertion")

    def helper_check(self):
        assert True


# test_neg has two runs of five: the longest is 5.
def test_neg():
    assert 1 == 1
    assert 2 == 2
    assert 3 == 3
    assert 4 == 4
    assert 5 == 5
    print("break")
    assert 1 == 1
    assert 2 == 2
    assert 3 == 3
    assert 4 == 4
    assert 5 == 5


# test_dup_a and test_dup_b share four identical assertions.
def test_dup_a():
    assert got.a == 1
    assert got.b == 2
    assert got.c == 3
    assert got.d == 4


def test_dup_b():
    assert got.a == 1
    assert got.b == 2
    assert got.c == 3
    assert got.d == 4
    check()


# test_near_a and test_near_b share only three identical assertions.
def test_near_a():
    assert want.a == 1
    assert want.b == 2
    assert want.c == 3
    assert want.d == 4


def test_near_b():
    assert want.a == 1
    assert want.b == 2
    assert want.c == 3
    assert want.e == 5


def not_a_test():
    assert True
